Explain the example for explain a result in words

blocks.text: A polite live region can announce a small update without moving keyboard focus. It is useful for a saved message or a count.

Try runnable HTML here with a keyboard as well as a mouse. A screen reader is a tool that reads page information aloud. Test real pages with people and tools; one automated check cannot prove everything works.

blocks.title: Explain a result in words

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `role="status"` lets a reading tool announce a changed message politely without moving focus to it.
`textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`querySelector` finds the first matching element. Check for a missing result when the element is optional.

blocks.text: The click adds a status message. A screen reader can announce it when it is ready.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not use a live region for every changing word. Too many announcements are hard to follow.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the status message to a short, clear result.
